name: Justice Corrigan
description: Concurred, argued that challenges to criminal fines should be reviewed under excessive fines clauses, and mandatory ancillary costs require consideration of a defendant's inability to pay due to equal protection.

name: Acting Chief Justice Evans
description: Concurred with majority opinion and Justice Liu's concurring opinion.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred, argued that imposing ancillary costs on indigent criminal defendants without fee waivers violates equal protection, and punitive fees can be challenged under excessive fines clauses. Also raised unaddressed issues like the constitutionality of mandatory minimum restitution fines and the evaluation of ability to pay.

name: Justice Rothschild†
description: Dissented from the majority's holding that imposing assessments without determining the defendant's ability to pay violates equal protection, arguing there is a rational basis for treating criminal and civil litigants differently. Concurred with the rest of the court's opinion.

name: Chief Justice Guerrero
description: Concurred, authored the opinion clarifying that constitutional bail provisions can be reconciled, and that pretrial bail must be reasonably attainable, not set above a defendant's ability to pay, to protect the right to pretrial release and equal protection.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and Justice Groban's concurring opinion.

name: Justice Groban
description: Concurred, argued that the Constitution limits pretrial detention to specific circumstances and that setting unattainable bail is effectively unconstitutional detention, but noted that courts have tools to manage public safety and flight risks.

name: Justice Evans
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and Justice Groban's concurring opinion.

name: Justice Wiley
description: Concurred, argued that the court's decision highlights the need for legislative and executive branches to develop a comprehensive bail system, as they are better equipped for broad policy-making than the judiciary.

name: Chief Justice Guerrero
description: Concurred, authored the court's opinion upholding the pronouns provision as a regulation of discriminatory conduct, not speech, and also filed a separate concurring opinion further elaborating on its constitutionality under strict scrutiny.

name: Justice Corrigan
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and Chief Justice Guerrero's separate concurring opinion.

name: Justice Groban
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and Chief Justice Guerrero's separate concurring opinion.

name: Justice Kruger
description: Concurred, arguing that the Court of Appeal's decision should be reversed solely due to a mistaken statutory interpretation, without addressing broader constitutional questions.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred with Justice Kruger's separate concurring opinion.

name: Chief Justice Guerrero
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, arguing that while admissible evidence is not strictly required for pretrial detention, the evidence considered must be reliable to protect an arrestee's fundamental right to pretrial liberty, and the 'assume truth of charges' instruction does not apply.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred, argued that the Taxpayer Protection and Government Accountability Act (TPA) constitutes an impermissible constitutional revision because it would fundamentally restructure governmental powers, including the Legislature's ability to levy taxes and delegate fee-setting authority, and expand referendum power, thus exceeding the scope of a citizen initiative.

name: Justice Corrigan
description: Concurred, argued that the officers' detention of Flores was unauthorized because his behavior, even if 'odd' or 'evasive,' did not provide reasonable suspicion of criminal activity under the Fourth Amendment, and individuals have the right to decline police interaction.

name: Justice Evans
description: Concurred, argued that attempts to avoid police contact must be viewed with care, acknowledging that 'nervous' or 'evasive' behavior can be a reasonable response for individuals, especially minorities, due to historical and ongoing issues of police violence and racial profiling, and should not automatically justify detention.

name: Kruger, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a trial court's discretion to grant relief from jury waiver is not solely based on hardship, and actual prejudice must be shown on appeal for reversal after a valid waiver.

name: Ashmann-Gerst, J.
description: Dissented, argued that denying relief from jury waiver without showing hardship was an abuse of discretion and warranted reversal without needing to show actual prejudice.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred, argued that Business and Professions Code section 7451, enacted by Proposition 22, does not conflict with article XIV, section 4 of the California Constitution, as the Legislature's plenary power is not exclusive and does not preclude the electorate's initiative power.

name: JENKINS, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that Measure Z contradicts state law by usurping the state supervisor's authority to regulate oil production methods, which are deemed suitable for increasing hydrocarbon recovery.

name: SEGAL, J.
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, which affirmed the duty to plead prior strikes and special circumstances allegations, but found no duty to prove prior strikes or to move to dismiss on a case-by-case basis.

name: LIU, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Oakland failed to demonstrate that the franchise fees are exempt from voter approval requirements under Proposition 26.

name: Jenkins, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's discussion on whether 'local government property' refers to physical objects was unnecessary to the resolution of the case.

name: CORRIGAN, J.
description: Concurred with the judgment, with limitations on the majority's discussion regarding 'local government property' and Exemption 1.

name: Liu, J.
description: Dissented, argued that denying in-person parole hearings to Proposition 57-eligible inmates likely violates due process, and the issue is of statewide importance warranting review.

name: Cantil-Sakauye, C. J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Department's regulation excluding inmates serving a term for a violent felony from early parole consideration is valid and consistent with Proposition 57.

name: LIU, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Department's regulation is a reasonable construction of the constitutional provision, but noted questions remain about the proper application of the regulation to inmates with both violent and nonviolent felony offenses.

name: KRUGER, J.
description: Concurred with Justice Liu's concurring opinion.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred, but expressed doubts about the constitutionality of California's death penalty scheme in light of Apprendi and its progeny, urging reexamination of the issue of jury unanimity and reasonable doubt for aggravating factors.

name: Justice Cuéllar
description: Concurred, argued that conditioning pretrial release solely on an arrestee's ability to pay bail, without considering less restrictive alternatives or financial capacity, is unconstitutional, violating due process and equal protection.

name: Groban, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Senate Bill 1391 is a permissible amendment to Proposition 57, consistent with its fundamental purposes of promoting rehabilitation and reducing the prison population.

name: Cuéllar, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a finding of constitutionally excessive incarceration does not automatically terminate an inmate's statutory parole period, and therefore reversed the Court of Appeal's judgment.

name: Justice Liu
description: Concurred, argued that a finding of excessive incarceration should necessarily prevent reincarceration for parole violations and that the Court of Appeal's decision to terminate parole might have been an individualized conclusion, not an automatic rule.
